prompt:
Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1440
Claimant:
Tonya Compton
Adjuster:
Chelsea Hebert
2025-05-22
The claim was opened after the insured reported a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection, and the claimant's
attorney has since notified us of representation. Initial contact with the claimant has been routed through counsel.
2025-06-21
The driver of the insured vehicle is a resident of the policyholder's household and is listed as a covered household
member under the policy. Coverage eligibility has been confirmed for this loss.
2025-07-02
Scene photographs were received and show the rear bumper, tail lamp assembly, and trunk lid damage consistent
with the reported impact. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos are the main visual record of
the event.
2025-07-16
The police report and statements from the parties confirm the claimant was present in the vehicle at the time of the
collision. No earlier damage to the claimant's vehicle has come to light in our review of prior claims and inspection
records.
2025-09-15
Medical records show a diagnosis of a neck strain, which fits the type and force of a rear-end impact of this kind. No
prior injury to the neck or upper back has been identified in the claimant's records.
2025-10-23
Treatment has followed a typical course, with therapy visits tapering as the claimant's range of motion improved. It is
not yet clear whether all of the vehicle damage in the repair estimate resulted from this impact, so the supplement is
under review.
2025-11-14
The claimant has given the same account of the collision in each conversation, including through counsel. Nothing in
the file suggests that the damage occurred before the coverage period began.
2025-11-24
Next steps are to request the remaining treatment billing through counsel and to complete the damage review with
the repair shop before the valuation is finalized.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
JSON format:
